html:
"Suomi" is the map's label, for 1000, for Finland Proper, the region of southwest Finland around today's Turku. Suomi is the Finnish name of the whole country, but it first meant this corner.

It was the most settled and farmed part of Finland in the late Iron Age, with many villages along the coast and rivers and close links across the sea to Sweden. Its people were one branch of the Finns, with the Tavastians inland and the Karelians to the east. In the 1100s and 1200s Swedish kings and the church came in; the tale of a crusade by King Eric and Bishop Henry is told of this time. Turku became the seat of the bishop, and the region was the core of Swedish Finland.
